summary_rationale: MCX operates a near-monopoly (>99% domestic market share) in Indian non-agricultural commodity derivatives across bullion, energy, and base metals, reinforced by the central counterparty network effects of MCXCCL and a ₹1,367.29 crore Settlement Guarantee Fund. Following the October 2023 migration from 63 Moons to the TCS Commodity Derivatives Platform, technology expenses stabilized into a predictable ₹104.74 crore annual band, unlocking extraordinary operating leverage: FY26 operating revenue doubled to ₹2,302 crore with 71% operating margins, 71.4% ROCE, and ₹3,035 crore in operating cash flow, followed by Q2 FY27 revenue of ₹800 crore and 76% operating margins as options notional ADT scaled to ₹12.00 lakh crore and active F&O clients reached 14.98 lakh. It earns COMPOUNDER_PASS for its asset-light toll-booth economics and structural deepening of domestic hedging, paired with PASS_WITH_WATCH on KPIs due to high concentration in bullion/energy options, sensitivity to commodity volatility regimes, regulatory risk from SEBI derivatives guardrails, and operational resilience scrutiny after the October 2025 four-hour UCC capacity outage.
